package: W50-01 — durable worktree archive intent and power-loss recovery
question: Can a power loss between the archive rename and the worktree removal be reconciled later?
answer: Yes. A durable intent written before the rename lets the next start or removal restore the archived history into an unchanged checkout, clear a completed removal, and retain anything ambiguous.

sourcePosition.kind: local extension; archive layout has no recovered body
sourcePosition.evidence: recovered zPo (chunk-sfn1dbxq.js [1801370,1802540), UTF-8 bytes) reconciles stale state at observation time and retains what it cannot prove.

behavior.write: before the history rename: fsync .agent/worktree-history/.pending-<uuid>.json with origin, checkout, history, archive, checkout dev/ino, pid, created_at
behavior.rollback: an in-process restore deletes the intent; an intent is kept when the archive remains and the checkout still exists
behavior.recovery: interactive start and every removal run recoverWorktreeArchives: restore into an unchanged checkout, clear completed/already-home intents, retain ambiguous states with warnings

changes.change: power-loss recovery case and no-pending assertions
three C-4 rows record the completed archive recovery
worktree relocation row records the intent and recovery

tests.added: an archive intent left by a power loss is reconciled on the next start

residuals: A crash before the intent rename leaves a .pending-<uuid>.json.<uuid>.tmp file; recovery ignores it because it carries no owner.
Ambiguous states (history and archive both present, changed checkout identity, invalid intent) are retained for inspection.
Headless single-shot runs do not reconcile archives until an interactive start or another removal in that workspace.
The scan is capped at 100 intents per workspace.
